# BITE WOUNDS WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS

---

## BITE WOUNDS

Bite wounds are prone to infection because of the pathogenic oral flora carried into tissues by teeth. Clean wounds with soap and water as soon as possible.
Consult Orthopedic surgery for bite wounds involving the hand.

## Antibiotic Prophylaxis Indications:

Severe injury less than 8 hours, Crush injury, Bone or joint penetration, Wound of the face or hands or genitals, Immunocompromised host, Asplenia, Advanced liver disease
*Routine use of prophylactic antibiotics for non-immunocompromised patients with superficial wounds with no puncture that do not involve the face/ genitals/hands is not recommended.

## Antimicrobial Treatment:

Empiric treatment for suspected or established infection following bite wound In these cases, therapy should be directed against pathogen identified by Gram stain and culture whenever possible.

## Rabies Prophylaxis:

Consider rabies post-exposure prophylaxis for all animal bite cases. Contact Infectious diseases for assistance.

## Consider tetanus immunization status:

If immunization is up to date, nothing more needs to be done to prevent tetanus.
If immunization is lacking, and: wound IS NOT tetanus prone, bring immunization up to date with Td wound IS tetanus prone, bring immunization up to date with Td < AND > Human Tetanus Immune Globulin Inject 250 units deeply into muscle (deep IM)

## Select below for Tetanus vaccination information page:

[Tetanus, Diphtheria and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine Information Page](tetanus-diphtheria-and-acellular-pertussis-vaccine-information)

## Prophylaxis:

Duration 3 to 5 days:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 5 days [R]
Non-VA order for above
